objectives: Explain why notaries are obliged persons and which measures they apply.
Decide when customer due diligence is required, using the thresholds of the law.
Identify a natural person, a legal entity and its beneficial owner, and record the data.
Recognise a politically exposed person and the enhanced measures that follow.
Report a suspicion correctly and avoid tipping off the client.

cards.front: Are notaries obliged persons under the AML Act?
cards.back: **Yes**: notaries and substitute assistant notaries ([[zmip:4::14|Art. 4 item 14 ЗМИП]]).

cards.front: What is the threshold for due diligence in an occasional deal?
A buyer pays 4,000 euro in cash for a garage. Is due diligence required?
cards.back: **Not by the amount**: the cash threshold is 5,000 euro ([[zmip:11:1:3|Art. 11(1) item 3 ЗМИП]]). Any suspicion requires it regardless of the amount (item 6).

cards.front: When is due diligence required regardless of the amount?
cards.back: In every case of **suspicion**, and when there is **doubt about the identification data** ([[zmip:11:1:6|Art. 11(1) items 6]] and [[zmip:11:1:7|7 ЗМИП]]).

cards.front: What data does the office collect about a natural person?
cards.back: Names; date and place of birth; identity number from a valid document with a photo; all citizenships; country of residence and address ([[zmip:53]]).
The **natural person** who ultimately owns or controls the client ([[zmip:59]]; § 2 of the additional provisions).

cards.front: When is a beneficial owner declaration required?
cards.back: When the register data and the documents are **insufficient or contradictory** ([[zmip:59:1:3|Art. 59(1) item 3 ЗМИП]]).

cards.front: How is the origin of funds clarified?
cards.back: By at least **two** methods of the act; by a **written declaration** when they fail or contradict each other ([[zmip:66]]).

cards.front: The buyer is the deputy mayor of a municipality. What follows?
cards.back: **Enhanced due diligence**: mayors and deputy mayors of municipalities and districts are politically exposed persons ([[zmip:36:2:9|Art. 36(2) item 9 ЗМИП]]).

cards.front: Can the PEP check rely only on the client's declaration?
How long are AML records kept?
When must a suspicion be reported, and to whom?
cards.back: **At once, before the deal**, to the **Financial Intelligence Directorate of SANS** ([[zmip:72:1]]).

cards.front: For how long can the directorate suspend a deal?
cards.back: Up to **5 working days** from the day after the order ([[zmip:73:1]]).

cards.front: A client asks: "Did you report me?" What may the office say?
cards.back: **Nothing about a report**: the office, the notary and the employees may not tell the client or third persons about a report ([[zmip:80:1]]).

quiz.question: A buyer pays 4,000 euro in cash for a garage. Is due diligence required?
options: No; the cash threshold is 5,000 euro
Yes; cash always requires due diligence
No; a garage is below every threshold
Yes; every real estate deal requires it
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:11:1:3|Art. 11(1) item 3 ЗМИП]]: an occasional deal paid in cash requires due diligence from 5,000 euro; 4,000 euro is below it. Item 6: a suspicion requires it regardless of the amount, so the clerk still watches for warning signs.

quiz.question: A sale of a flat for 95,000 euro by bank transfer. Is due diligence required?
options: Yes; the occasional deal is 15,000 euro or more
No; payments by bank transfer are exempt from the check
Yes, but only for the seller of the flat
Only when the buyer is a foreign citizen
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:11:1:2|Art. 11(1) item 2 ЗМИП]]: an occasional deal of 15,000 euro or more requires due diligence, whatever the way of payment and the citizenship of the parties. Both parties are identified ([[zmip:53|Art. 53]]).

quiz.question: The client's identity card looks altered; the deal is for 3,000 euro by transfer. Is due diligence required?
options: Yes; doubt about the identification data requires it
No; the deal is below every threshold of the law
No; the office only refuses the act and notes nothing
Only if the client cannot show a second document
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:11:1:7|Art. 11(1) item 7 ЗМИП]]: due diligence is required when there is doubt about the truth or the adequacy of the identification data, whatever the amount; item 6 adds any suspicion. The office records the check and reports when the doubt becomes a suspicion ([[zmip:72|Art. 72]]).

quiz.question: A company buys an office. The register lists no beneficial owner. What does the office do?
options: Collects documents and a declaration of the representative
Proceeds; the register is the only source that the law requires
Treats the manager as the beneficial owner by default
Refuses the deal with every company without an entry
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:59:1]]: the beneficial owner is identified from the register (item 1) and from documents (item 2); when the information is insufficient, a declaration by the legal representative or agent is required (item 3). The manager is not the owner by default.

quiz.question: The buyer is the deputy mayor of a city. What follows?
options: Enhanced due diligence, as a politically exposed person
Nothing special; local officials are not covered by the act
The deal is refused; officials may not buy property
Only a declaration that the money is his own
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:36:2:9|Art. 36(2) item 9 ЗМИП]]: mayors and deputy mayors of municipalities and districts and chairs of municipal councils are politically exposed persons; [[zmip:36:1|Art. 36(1)]] requires enhanced due diligence for them and for their related persons. The deal is not prohibited.

quiz.question: How may the office establish that a client is not a politically exposed person?
options: An internal system; a declaration alone is not enough
The client's declaration alone, kept in the file
A question to the municipality where the client lives
No check; the client states it when asked
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:42:3]]: the finding whether a client is a politically exposed person may not rest only on the client's declaration; the office uses its internal system and other sources together with the declaration.

quiz.question: A clerk suspects that the buyer's money comes from a crime. What must the office do?
options: Reports to the directorate before the deal and delays it
Tells the buyer and asks him to explain the money
Performs the deal and reports to the directorate within one month
Calls the bank of the buyer and asks about the funds
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:72:1]]: on a suspicion of money laundering or funds of criminal origin, the obliged person notifies the Financial Intelligence Directorate of SANS at once, before the deal, and delays the deal within the permitted term. Telling the buyer is tipping off ([[zmip:80|Art. 80]]).

quiz.question: The suspicion arises only after the deed is signed and entered. What does the office do?
options: Reports at once after the deal, stating why a delay was impossible
Does not report; the duty applies only before the deal
Reports within one month, with a copy of the deed and the file attached
Asks the registry office to cancel the entry of the deed
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:72:2]]: when a delay of the deal is objectively impossible, the obliged person notifies the directorate at once after the deal and states the reasons; [[zmip:72:5|Art. 72(5)]]: the duty exists also when the deal was not completed.

quiz.question: The client asks: "Did you report me?" What may the clerk say?
options: Nothing about a report; tipping off is prohibited
Yes, we did; the law requires honesty with the client
No, we did not; a denial protects the report
That the notary will call the agency for the client
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:80:1]]: the obliged persons, their managers and their employees may not inform the client or third persons about a report. The clerk neither confirms nor denies; a false denial is also information about the report.

quiz.question: The buyer cannot document his savings, and two methods give contradictory information. What does the office ask for?
options: A written declaration of the origin of the funds
Nothing; two methods of the act were already applied
A bank guarantee for the price of the deal
A court decision that the money is lawful
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:66:1]]: the origin of funds is clarified by at least two of the listed methods; [[zmip:66:2|Art. 66(2)]]: when they fail or give contradictory information, by a written declaration of the client or the representative. The declaration is kept in the file ([[zmip:66:3|Art. 66(3)]]).

quiz.question: Who performs internal AML control in a small notary office?
options: The notary personally, or a designated senior employee
The Notary Chamber, through its regional college of notaries
The bank of the office, as a credit institution
Nobody; small offices are exempt from the control
quiz.explanation: [[zmip:107:1|Art. 107(1)]]–[[zmip:107:3|(3) ЗМИП]] (in force 1 July 2026): the notary creates a specialised service or performs the internal control personally, and may designate in writing an employee in a senior position; the directorate is informed of that employee ([[zmip:107:4|Art. 107(4)]]).

quiz.question: A client asks to pay 12,000 euro in three cash instalments of 4,000 euro "to stay under the limit". What is the right view?
options: Related payments add up; the request is a warning sign
Allowed; each payment is below the cash limit
Allowed, with a declaration of the origin of the funds in the deed
Allowed; the limit applies to leva, not to euro
quiz.explanation: [[zopvb:3:1:1|Art. 3(1) items 1]] and [[zopvb:3:1:2|2 ЗОПБ]]: payments of 10,000 лв. or more, and smaller payments that are part of related operations on the same ground, go through a payment account; the limit covers foreign currency ([[zopvb:3:2|Art. 3(2)]]). Splitting to avoid a threshold is a ground for suspicion under [[zmip:11:1:6|Art. 11(1) item 6 ЗМИП]].
